audit_findings.title: The anchor is stale because FY2025 was lost in extraction
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (filed FY2025 operating cash flow less capital expenditures was $41.4 million versus the $133.1 million FY2024 anchor, but this is not a rail-equivalent OE calculation; the June 2026 cash bridge also contains $338.9 million of Feminine Care sale proceeds)
audit_findings.mechanism: The missing FY2025 OE changes the earnings anchor and growth basis. The FY2024 anchor also predates the Feminine Care divestiture, while the June 2026 bridge includes the sale proceeds, creating a risk that earnings from the sold business and its sale value are both counted.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to incur restructuring charges of approximately $29 in fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated dating and perimeter error, not merely a possibility: an audited FY2025 10-K exists, but the valuation calls FY2024 the latest actual. The record also shows weaker FY2025 cash generation and materially weaker continuing-operation performance through June 2026. Because the anchor drives the entire operating valuation and may include a business already converted into bridge cash, the error is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Calculate FY2025 OE under the identical owner-earnings rails, construct a continuing-operations OE perimeter excluding Feminine Care, reconcile the $338.9 million sale proceeds and approximately $55 million of sale taxes, incorporate material FY2026 year-to-date operating changes, and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: June-quarter cash may be seasonal operating cash rather than distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $397.1 million added to the bridge, equal to 18.3% of the $2,166.0 million base equity value; approximately $55 million of sale taxes alone equals $1.12 per valuation share and would reduce the buy-below price by about $0.78
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for taxes, seasonal working capital, minimum liquidity, restricted foreign balances, or operations is not excess cash and should not be added dollar-for-dollar in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our cash flows are affected by the seasonality of our Sun Care business, typically resulting in higher net sales and increased cash generated in the second and third quarter of each fiscal year.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the June balance occurs during a cash-generative seasonal period, includes proceeds from the February 2026 divestiture, and precedes approximately $55 million of expected sale taxes. The $55 million known use alone does not reverse the stated buy conclusion, but the valuation adds the entire balance without an excess-cash test. Because the full bridge amount is $8.06 per valuation share and removing a sufficiently large operating portion would move the buy-below threshold below the $28.87 market price, the unresolved excess-cash amount is material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $397.1 million from September 2025 through post-season fiscal year-end, deduct the approximately $55 million sale-tax payment and other committed uses, establish minimum operating liquidity, quantify accessible foreign cash and repatriation costs, and rerun the bridge using only distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Required pension funding is a senior non-debt claim absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.9 million combined pension and postretirement net deficit at September 30, 2025; $16.5 million of projected U.S. pension contributions for fiscal 2026-2030
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash funding exceeding pension expense would reduce OE, or an otherwise unreflected funded-status deficit would reduce the equity bridge once, with no double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: The projected contributions for the U.S. pension plans total $ 6.5 in fiscal 2025, $ 7.0 in fiscal 2026, $ 5.0 in fiscal 2027, $ 4.5 in fiscal 2028, and $ 4.2 in fiscal 2029.
audit_findings.explanation: The updated filing narrows the issue materially: the September 2025 pension deficit was $5.2 million and the postretirement deficit was $4.7 million. Their $9.9 million total is 0.46% of base equity value, or about $0.20 per valuation share. Even the full $16.5 million of disclosed fiscal 2026-2030 contributions is only 0.76% of base equity value, about $0.33 per share, and would reduce the buy-below threshold by about $0.23 if treated entirely as an incremental bridge deduction. That scale cannot by itself overturn the stated price conclusion.

audit_findings.title: Recurring receivables-sale costs could be mistaken for purgeable financing income
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.4 million pre-tax in FY2024; if the entire amount were wrongly removed from the $133.1 million anchor, it would equal 4.8% of anchor OE and approximately $85.1 million or $1.73 per share of base operating value before tax adjustment
audit_findings.mechanism: Improperly purging the factoring loss from other income would increase anchor OE and every forecast cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: For the years ended September 30, 2024 and 2023, the loss on sale of trade receivables was $ 6.4 and $ 6.2 , respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring economic cost is demonstrated, but its removal from OE is not: the filed loss was $6.4 million in FY2024, $5.6 million in FY2025, and $3.2 million for the first nine months of FY2026. The valuation record does not show whether the portfolio-interest purge retained or removed it. Its possible base-value effect is meaningful and relatively close to the valuation's price-to-buy-below cushion, but tax treatment and the actual OE mapping are absent, so the record cannot establish materiality conclusively.
audit_findings.action: Trace the FY2024 $6.4 million loss through the OE worksheet and purge entries; if it was removed, restore the after-tax operating cost, verify the same treatment for FY2025 and FY2026, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The latest-actual anchor may retain a discrete plant-fire loss
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.2 million pre-tax and $9.2 million after tax in FY2024; the filed after-tax amount equals 6.9% of anchor OE and approximately $122.3 million or $2.48 per share of base value under proportional DCF scaling
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining a nonrecurring fire cost reduces anchor OE and all forecast cash flows; removing associated costs without netting insurance recoveries would have the opposite effect.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2024, we incurred $12.2 in incremental costs related to material charges, increased labor and absorption and other inefficiency costs as a result of the fire.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing identifies the $12.2 million charge separately, reports a $9.2 million after-tax effect, shows no corresponding fire charge in FY2025, and attributes subsequent Wet Ones sales improvement to recovery from the prior disruption. If the charge remains in the anchor, the valuation is conservative: normalizing the filed after-tax amount would increase the base value by about $2.48 per share and the buy-below threshold by about $1.74. It therefore cannot overturn the existing buy conclusion adversely, although it matters to the precise value estimate and must not be adjusted without checking insurance proceeds.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $12.2 million cost and any insurance proceeds through FY2024 OE, confirm normalization from FY2025 operating evidence, and apply a net after-tax adjustment only when rebuilding the superseding FY2025/perimeter-consistent anchor.
